```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

Code accompanying: Trachtenberg, E., Mousley, A., Jelen, M., & Astle, D. *Mapping social functioning profiles across childhood neurodevelopmental difficulties: links with diagnosis, cognition, and everyday executive function.*

This file covers the first step of the pipeline (Figure 1). Social behaviour and peer relationship items were drawn from three parent-report questionnaires collected within CALM (Holmes et al., 2019): the SDQ, CCC-2 and Conners-3. Twenty-two items indexing social functioning were selected (Table S1). Item-level relationships were modelled using a regularised partial correlation network (EBICglasso), and communities were identified using Louvain modularity optimisation to derive the social dimensions.

**Data availability.** No data are included in this repository; the code is shared to show the analysis. CALM data are available via the [CALM data portal](https://portal.camide.cam.ac.uk/overview/1158), subject to the cohort's data access procedures.

# Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(polycor)    # hetcor()
library(corrplot)
library(qgraph)     # EBICglasso(), network plot
library(igraph)     # Louvain and Walktrap community detection
```

# Load and merge questionnaires

CALM data come in two batches (CALM 200 and CALM 800), which are combined for each questionnaire.

```{r}
sdq200      <- read.csv("CALM200-Assessments-calm200_sdq.csv", fileEncoding = "ISO-8859-1")
sdq800      <- read.csv("Assessments-sdq.csv", fileEncoding = "ISO-8859-1")
ccc200      <- read.csv("CALM200-Assessments-calm200_ccc2.csv", fileEncoding = "ISO-8859-1")
ccc800      <- read.csv("Assessments-ccc2.csv", fileEncoding = "ISO-8859-1")
conners200  <- read.csv("CALM200-Assessments-calm200_conners.csv", fileEncoding = "ISO-8859-1")
conners800  <- read.csv("Assessments-conners.csv", fileEncoding = "ISO-8859-1")

# Column 34 is named differently in the two CCC-2 batches
colnames(ccc800)[34] <- "ccc2_valid"
stopifnot(all(colnames(ccc200) == colnames(ccc800)))

sdq_all     <- rbind(sdq200, sdq800)
ccc_all     <- rbind(ccc200, ccc800)
conners_all <- rbind(conners200, conners800)

allscales_df <- sdq_all %>%
  full_join(ccc_all, by = "id") %>%
  full_join(conners_all, by = "id")
```

# Social items (Table S1)

```{r}
item_groups <- list(
  SDQ     = c("sdq1", "sdq4", "sdq9", "sdq17", "sdq20",
              "sdq6", "sdq11", "sdq14", "sdq19", "sdq23"),
  CCC2    = c("ccc2_3", "ccc2_7", "ccc2_13", "ccc2_16", "ccc2_33", "ccc2_57", "ccc2_67"),
  Conners = c("conners4", "conners6", "conners18", "conners38", "conners43")
)
soc_items <- unlist(item_groups, use.names = FALSE)

socitems_df <- allscales_df %>%
  dplyr::select(id, all_of(soc_items)) %>%
  mutate(across(-id, as.numeric))

nrow(socitems_df)
```

# Missing data

Missing values were 2% or less per item and were replaced with the item mean.

```{r}
round(colMeans(is.na(socitems_df[soc_items])) * 100, 1)

socitems_imp <- socitems_df %>%
  mutate(across(-id, ~ replace_na(.x, mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))))
```

# Harmonising response scales

The questionnaires use different response scales, so each item was z-scored and then rescaled to the 0-1 range.

```{r}
z_score <- function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
rescale_0_1 <- function(x) (x - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) - min(x, na.rm = TRUE))

socitems_z <- socitems_imp %>%
  mutate(across(-id, z_score))

socitems_harmonised <- socitems_z %>%
  mutate(across(-id, ~ round(rescale_0_1(.x), 2)))

item_data <- socitems_harmonised %>% dplyr::select(-id)
```

# Item correlations

```{r, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 9}
item_cor <- hetcor(item_data)$correlations

corrplot(item_cor, method = "color", type = "upper",
         tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45)
```

# Regularised partial correlation network (Figure S1)

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
network <- EBICglasso(item_cor, n = nrow(item_data), gamma = 0.5, threshold = TRUE)

# Node groups by questionnaire (indices, in the order of the network columns)
node_groups <- lapply(item_groups, function(items) match(items, colnames(item_data)))

qgraph(network,
       layout = "spring",
       labels = colnames(item_data),
       label.cex = 4,
       label.prop = 0.6,
       edge.labels = FALSE,
       minimum = 0.07,          # display only: hides very weak edges
       groups = node_groups,
       color = c("lightblue", "red", "orange"),
       vsize = 7,
       legend = TRUE)
```

# Louvain community detection

Communities were identified on the absolute edge weights.

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
graph_abs <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(abs(network), mode = "undirected",
                                         weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)

set.seed(42)   # Louvain uses a random node order
louvain <- cluster_louvain(graph_abs)

cat("Louvain modularity Q =", round(modularity(louvain), 3), "\n")

communities <- tibble(item = colnames(item_data),
                      community = as.vector(membership(louvain))) %>%
  arrange(community)
communities

plot(graph_abs,
     vertex.color = rainbow(max(membership(louvain)))[membership(louvain)],
     vertex.size = 8,
     vertex.label.cex = 1.2,
     edge.width = E(graph_abs)$weight * 5,
     main = "Louvain communities")
```

# Robustness check: Walktrap

```{r}
walktrap <- cluster_walktrap(graph_abs)
cat("Walktrap modularity Q =", round(modularity(walktrap), 3), "\n")

communities %>%
  mutate(walktrap = as.vector(membership(walktrap))[match(item, colnames(item_data))])
```
